title: Stack push and pop
instructorPromptText: Write a C program that implements a Stack data structure using a linked list. Implement `push` and `pop` functions. The program should push 3 integers onto the stack and pop them one by one, printing each popped value.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the `pop` function handle stack underflow (empty stack) gracefully by returning a sentinel value or printing an error, instead of crashing?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Underflow condition checks are critical when popping or removing elements from any dynamic data structure.

specGateDimensions.description: Are pointers properly reassigned inside `push` and `pop` to ensure the stack top changes correctly?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Verifies that the student correctly links and unlinks nodes, which tests their manipulation of pointer references.

specGateDimensions.description: Does `pop` call `free` on the node being removed after extracting its data?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Unlike print-only operations, popping elements requires deallocating that specific node's memory to avoid accumulation leaks.

expectedDivergences.pattern: Student forgets to call `free` on the popped node inside the `pop` function.
Student dereferences the top pointer when it is NULL in `pop`, leading to a segmentation fault.
Student implements stack using a fixed-size array instead of the requested linked list structure.
Student creates a helper struct `Stack` containing the top pointer to bundle state, rather than using a naked `Node*` pointer.
Student loses the reference to the next node when updating the top pointer, making subsequent pops fail.
